subject.title: refactor(ui): use Web Awesome controls throughout Control UI

question: After the wizard regression is fixed and real behavior proof is posted, should Control UI adopt Web Awesome 3.10.0 as its canonical composite-control layer with the proposed startup-budget increases?
rationale: The patch deliberately exchanges extensive homegrown interaction code for a third-party component runtime and larger startup ceilings; tests can verify behavior, but only an owner can accept that long-term dependency and performance tradeoff.

options.title: Accept after repair and proof
options.body: Fix the default-selection dead end, provide real browser evidence, and merge after confirming the dependency graph and measured startup cost.

options.title: Split the migration
options.body: Land smaller control families independently so each dependency, behavior, and performance increment can be reviewed and proven separately.

options.title: Pause the dependency migration
options.body: Keep the merged keyboard/focus foundation and defer replacing the remaining homegrown controls until the dependency and payload tradeoff is reconsidered.

recommendation.title: Accept after repair and proof
recommendation.body: Fix the default-selection dead end, provide real browser evidence, and merge after confirming the dependency graph and measured startup cost.

likelyOwner.reason: The prior merged accessibility foundation and canonical issue establish direct ownership of this Control UI direction.
